/.title: OpenGenie — a Databricks coding agent with the model you choose
/.description: Genie Code gives you one model and a metered bill. OpenGenie is an Apache-2.0 Databricks App that does the same work with 16 models, a write fence, and proof before it says done.

tour/.title: Tour — what OpenGenie looks like
tour/.description: The app at four widths and in both themes: the notebook, the assistant dock bound to it, the model picker, and the fence.

images.alt: The shell at 1440 px: a left rail listing sessions and files, a notebook with four cells in the centre, and the assistant dock on the right headed 'in context: parity_demo'.
The shell at 800 px: the left rail and the assistant are collapsed into buttons, and the notebook takes the full width.
A notebook named parity_demo with two markdown-free SQL cells, each showing Ask and Run buttons, and a bar above with Run all and the warehouse name.
A notebook after Run all: two cells succeeded, the third shows an error from the SQL engine, and a button labelled Fix with agent sits beside it.
A prompt open on cell three with the placeholder naming that cell, and chips for Explain, Fix, Optimise and Comment.
The assistant dock showing the sent message, with a chip reading cell 3 and a sentence saying to change only that cell.
The dock scrolled to the end of a turn, with three follow-up chips under the answer.
The dock after Fix with agent: the sent message quotes the SQL engine's error and is bound to cell four.
The model picker open over the shell, listing models grouped by provider with their context and output limits.
The workspace tree open, showing folders and notebooks, with a chooser for the working folder.
A session opened on a notebook: the dock is headed with the notebook name and offers three starter questions.
The same session at 800 px, with the assistant available as a drawer over the notebook.
The notebook and the assistant in dark theme, with the in-cell prompt open and readable.
A markdown cell rendering LaTeX as typeset mathematics in dark theme.
The same LaTeX rendering at a narrow width, with the formula still legible and no horizontal scroll on the page.
The composer with a slash typed, showing a list of commands with descriptions.
A history popover over the dock: a search field, a day heading, and a list of conversations with the active one marked.
The shell with all zones visible, showing the working folder and the fence notice in the inspector.
